note: Contend: soul longs to hear salvation, soul rejoices, bereft(evil-for-good), costly compassion-for-enemies, mourning-for-them, thanks-in-assembly, delight-in-vindication, tell-righteousness

277461.gloss: say to my soul 'I am your salvation'

dims.v: say to my soul 'I am your salvation'
the self asks God to say to its soul, 'I am your salvation' - a longing to hear the inner assurance spoken
v3: 'Say to my SOUL, I am your SALVATION!' - the operation is a craving not just for rescue but for the word of it: the interior wants God to address its soul directly.

277482.gloss: my soul shall rejoice in his salvation

dims.v: my soul shall rejoice in his salvation
the self's soul will rejoice in the LORD, exulting in his salvation - anticipated inner joy
v9: 'Then my SOUL will REJOICE in the LORD, EXULTING in his salvation' - the operation leans forward into joy: the interior already tastes the gladness the rescue will bring.

277325.gloss: my soul bereft, repaid evil for good

dims.v: my soul bereft, repaid evil for good
the enemies repay evil for good, leaving the self's soul bereaved - the desolation of betrayed kindness
v12: 'They REPAY me EVIL for GOOD; my SOUL is BEREFT' - the operation is the specific wound of ingratitude: the interior is emptied because its good was answered with harm.

277330.gloss: I afflicted myself when they were sick

dims.v: I afflicted myself when they were sick
when the enemies were sick, the self wore sackcloth, afflicted itself with fasting, and prayed with head bowed - costly compassion once shown to those who now repay evil

v13: 'But I, when they were sick - I wore sackcloth; I AFFLICTED myself with FASTING; I PRAYED with head bowed' - the operation is love spent on the very ones who now betray: the interior once grieved and interceded for its persecutors.

277341.gloss: I mourned for them as for kin

dims.v: I mourned for them as for kin
the self went about as though grieving for a friend or brother, bowed in mourning as for its mother - identifying with the enemies' suffering

v14: 'I went about as though I grieved for my friend or my brother; as one who LAMENTS his mother, I bowed down in MOURNING' - distinct from the fasting: this is the depth of felt grief, the interior mourning enemies as its closest family.

277364.gloss: I will thank you in the great congregation

dims.v: I will thank you in the great congregation
the self vows to thank God in the great congregation, to praise him among the mighty throng - gratitude discharged publicly
v18: 'I will THANK you in the great congregation; in the mighty throng I will PRAISE you' - the operation turns the anticipated rescue into a pledge of public thanksgiving.

277438.gloss: those who delight in my vindication

dims.v: those who delight in my vindication
the self asks that those who delight in its righteousness shout for joy and be glad, saying 'Great is the LORD' - the joy of those who love justice

v27: 'Let those who DELIGHT in my righteousness shout for JOY and be GLAD... Great is the LORD, who delights in the WELFARE of his servant' - the operation invokes a company whose interior is gladdened by the vindication of the right.

277451.gloss: my tongue shall tell your righteousness all day

dims.v: my tongue shall tell your righteousness all day
the self's tongue will tell of God's righteousness and praise all the day long - unceasing testimony

v28: 'Then my TONGUE shall TELL of your righteousness and of your praise all the day long' - the operation closes the psalm in perpetual proclamation; the vindicated interior will not stop speaking God's justice.
v3: 'Say to my soul, I am your SALVATION' - the assurance the soul longs to hear (God's own word).
v17: 'RESCUE me from their destruction, my precious life from the lions' - the deliverance the soul's rejoicing anticipates.
v24: 'VINDICATE me, O LORD my God, according to your righteousness' - the verdict that gladdens those who love the right.
